glosario.sol: A sol is one day on Mars. It lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
glosario.tormenta: A solar storm happens when the Sun sends energy and particles into space.
glosario.radiacion: Radiation is invisible energy that can harm the body. Dose is the amount received.
glosario.microgray: A microgray (µGy) is a unit for measuring absorbed radiation dose.
glosario.blindaje: Shielding is a layer that helps protect against radiation.
glosario.soporte: Life support includes the air and food the crew needs.
glosario.pronostico: A forecast is what scientists expect to happen. Its margin shows uncertainty, not a guarantee.
glosario.cme: A coronal mass ejection is a huge cloud of particles and magnetic fields released by the Sun. It can cause a storm.
glosario.rover: Curiosity is a NASA robot that has explored Mars since 2012.
guia.caminar: Go to the greenhouse marked in yellow. Use the arrow keys or tap the module.
guia.invernadero: In the greenhouse, press + until it has 4 units: this helps produce air and food.
guia.energia: Go to Power, marked in yellow, and give it 2 units with + to charge the shielding. Power is limited!
guia.refugio: Great. Go to the yellow shelter: when a storm arrives, the crew will be safer there.
bot.cientifico.invernadero: If you cut the greenhouse power, we will run out of food and fresh air tomorrow.
bot.cientifico.2: The greenhouse plants are getting cold. Give them power so they keep making oxygen!
bot.cientifico.3: Without light in the greenhouse, our Martian crops won't grow today.
bot.ingeniero.blindaje: If we don't reinforce the shelter shield today, there won't be time when the storm hits.
bot.ingeniero.2: The shelter shielding is still low. I need power in the panels to charge it in time!
bot.ingeniero.3: The solar storm is getting closer and the shelter still needs more protection.
panelModulo.desc.invernadero: The greenhouse provides food and oxygen for the crew.
panelModulo.desc.pasillo: Connects every module inside the Mars Dune Alpha base.
panelModulo.desc.energia: Solar panels charge the shelter's radiation shielding.
panelModulo.desc.refugio: Protects the crew during the solar storm.
panelModulo.desc.comunicaciones: Watches the Sun to give an early warning before the storm.
panelModulo.desc.enfermeria: Cares for the crew and tracks their radiation dose.
pausa.confirmar: Are you sure? Progress in this mission will be lost.
panelLateral.registro.vacio: No events recorded in this mission yet.
panelLateral.registro.inicio: Warning received: solar storm estimated in {horas} h (±{margen} h).
panelLateral.registro.peticionAceptada: You gave power to {modulo} after {quien}'s request.
panelLateral.registro.alertaRefugio: Early warning! Communications detected the imminent arrival of the storm.
panelLateral.registro.tormentaActiva: The solar storm hit the base! High radiation outside.
panelLateral.registro.finSuperada: The solar storm ended and the crew survived.
panelLateral.registro.finSinSoporte: Life support ran out before the mission ended.
reporte.curiosity: Curiosity measured radiation on Mars on May 20 and 21, 2024. Nobody lived there. The reference is the integrated dose over a roughly 31-hour window, not a measurement of your crew or necessarily the same duration as your game.
reporte.graficaAccesible: Chart of Curiosity radiation measurements from May 19 to 22. The measured peak was about 304 micrograys per hour on May 20. Gaps indicate incomplete data.
reporte.graficaNota: Hourly averages, May 19–22, 2024; timestamps interpreted as UTC. Gaps indicate incomplete data.
reporte.pronosticoNoDisponible: There is not enough data to compare this event's forecast.
fuentes.introduccion: The mission uses historical data and an imaginary base. Explore where each idea comes from.
fuentes.donki.texto: DONKI is NASA's database of space weather events, including coronal mass ejections. The game uses historical events stored locally.
fuentes.scoreboard.texto: The Earth CME Scoreboard compares forecasts with arrivals observed near Earth. The game uses those timings for its challenge; they are not arrivals measured at Mars. Some event associations are provisional.
fuentes.scoreboard.enlace: Learn about the Earth CME Scoreboard
fuentes.curiosity.texto: Curiosity measured radiation on Mars. RadLab samples from May 15 to 19 averaged about 4.115 µGy per hour. Integrating a selected window from May 20 to 21 gives around 1,645 µGy.
fuentes.curiosity.enlace: View Curiosity RAD in NASA RadLab
fuentes.sol.texto: A Martian day, or sol, lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes. The game rounds it to 24.65 hours.
fuentes.sol.enlace: Read about the length of a sol
fuentes.chapea.texto: CHAPEA is a NASA simulation on Earth with four people living in a habitat that imitates a Mars mission. Its roles include command, engineering, medicine and science; the game's crew is fictional.
fuentes.simplificado.texto: Energy, life support, shielding and crew doses use game rules and values. They are not NASA measurements or predictions. The base and its characters are imaginary.
inicio.subtitulo: You are the commander of a base on Mars. A solar storm is coming and the forecast isn't exact. When do you protect your crew?
inicio.honestidad: The storm is real: it happened in May 2024 and the Curiosity rover measured it. The crew is imaginary: nobody lives on Mars yet.
inicio.paso1: Walk around the base and enter each module.
inicio.paso2: Share the power: there's never enough for everything.
inicio.paso3: Listen to your crew, but you decide.
inicio.paso4: When the storm arrives, everyone to the shelter!
inicio.guia1.desc: Use the keyboard or tap any module to visit it.
inicio.guia2.desc: You get 10 bolts per day for oxygen, shield, and health.
inicio.guia3.desc: Forecasts can be off by hours. Get inside in time!
inicio.subtituloChapea: Educational simulator based on the CHAPEA program
bot.cientifico.critico1: Air and food are running out! The greenhouse needs power right now.
bot.cientifico.critico2: Commander, the plants are barely making oxygen. If we don't act, we won't make it!
bot.cientifico.comunicaciones1: Without power in Comms, we won't get Earth's alert when the storm is about to hit.
bot.cientifico.comunicaciones2: Earth can warn us a few hours before the storm… but only if the antenna has power.
bot.medico.alerta: Earth's alert just arrived! The storm is very close: everyone to the shelter.
bot.medico.fueraRefugio: Radiation went up and you're outside the shelter! Run, you'll be protected there.
bot.medico.enRefugio: Well done: we're in the shelter. Its walls protect us from radiation.
bot.ingeniero.sinAlerta: The storm hit without warning! With no power in Comms, we got no alert.
reporte.resultado.1: The storm caught them by surprise
reporte.explicaDias: To give you an idea: on a normal day on Mars, Curiosity measures about {dia} µGy of radiation. During a solar storm, that shoots up.
reporte.pronosticoAntes: This storm arrived {horas} hours EARLIER than the forecast said. It is a real error in NASA's forecast for the {fecha} eruption (measured near Earth, not at Mars).
reporte.pronosticoDespues: This storm arrived {horas} hours LATER than the forecast said. It is a real error in NASA's forecast for the {fecha} eruption (measured near Earth, not at Mars).
reporte.pronosticoExacto: This time the forecast was almost right: it was off by less than an hour. It is real NASA data for the {fecha} eruption (measured near Earth, not at Mars).
reporte.consejo.excelente: Excellent work! You charged the shielding in time and took the crew to the shelter.
reporte.consejo.soporte: Air and food ran out. Keep about 4 units of power in the greenhouse at all times.
reporte.consejo.blindaje: The shelter only had {pct}% shielding. Start charging it earlier: the storm can come early.
reporte.consejo.fueraRefugio: The shelter was ready, but you stayed outside during the storm. When the alarm sounds, run to the shelter!
reporte.consejo.comunicaciones: With no power in Comms there was no early alert. With 1 unit, Earth warns you a few hours ahead.
reporte.consejo.mejorar: Try charging the shielding a bit earlier: the forecast can be wrong by many hours.
glosario.tocaParaVer: Tap to see what it means
contexto.intro: You live in a Mars base with 3 fellow astronauts. Your job as captain is to keep them safe before a solar storm hits.
contexto.punto1: Walk around the base and enter modules to power them up.
contexto.punto2: Share your 10 power bolts between oxygen, shield, and health.
contexto.punto3: When the storm gets close, run with your crew to the Shelter!
